The JET tokamak has eight in-vessel antennas that actively excite stable AEs.
The Alfvén Eigenmode Active Diagnostic (AEAD) measures the frequencies, toroidal mode numbers, and net damping rates of AEs.
Over 1,000 AE stability measurements were collected in this study.
The study covers a range of effective ion masses from A = 1 (hydrogen) to A = 4 (helium).
Radiative damping is found to be a major contributor to AE stability.
The non-ideal parameter λ′ has a strong exponential dependence on radiative damping.
The edge safety factor q, edge magnetic shear s, and non-ideal parameter λ′ have strong positive correlations with AE damping rates.
The AEAD measures the effective ion mass by analyzing the frequencies of stable AEs.
Active MHD spectroscopy allows for the measurement of the effective ion mass and isotope ratio in hydrogenic plasmas.
The results suggest that AEs may be better stabilized in pre-fusion-power operations with H/He plasmas and therefore more readily destabilized in D/T campaigns.
The study finds that AE damping rates decrease with increasing effective ion mass, but increase for helium plasmas.
The Alfvén speed depends on the effective ion mass and the magnetic field strength.
The Alfvén frequency depends on the Alfvén speed and the mode structure and location.
The study uses a database of over 1,000 AE stability measurements to explore the effects of isotope composition on AE stability.
The results have implications for the design and operation of future fusion devices.
